LLM_description:
Situation:
Joint Task Force logistics are supporting dispersed combat units operating from multiple forward bases across contested terrain. Supply depots in the rear area are stocked but capacity is constrained by throughput and security posture. Ground lines of communication traverse valleys and choke points subject to enemy observation, IEDs, and intermittent indirect fire. Weather and route conditions limit convoy movement windows. Some outposts are only reachable via circuitous routes requiring engineer support and dedicated security elements.

Mission:
Deliver required supplies from rear depots to forward units while minimizing total operational cost, including transport costs, shortage penalties for unmet demand, vehicle deployment costs, and fixed route security risk costs. Ensure critical units maintain combat effectiveness and sustainment standards under current threat and mobility constraints.

Execution/Concept:
- Depot capacity: Outbound shipments will not exceed available stocks at each depot by supply type and time period.
- Demand fulfillment: Unit requirements will be met through allocated flows. Controlled shortfalls are allowed only where operationally acceptable and will accrue shortage penalties.
- Vehicle capacity: Loads must be consolidated within platform capacity. Supply classes have differing volume/weight factors that drive how many vehicles are required for each depot-to-unit movement.
- Route activation and risk: Vehicles may only move on routes that are activated. Activating any route (sending any vehicles on that segment) incurs a fixed Risk Cost that represents the security overhead—route clearance, escort teams, ISR coverage, and QRF staging—regardless of the number of vehicles dispatched on that route.
- Fleet size: Total vehicles employed across all routes must remain within available fleet. Prioritize convoy assignments to high-impact routes and consolidate flows to minimize repeated activations.
- Movement control: Sequence convoys to deconflict engineer clearance, air overwatch, and traffic on limited road networks. Favor lower-risk corridors when cost trade-offs are acceptable; accept controlled risk only where mission necessity dictates.
- Contingencies: If routes become denied or weather prevents movement, reallocate flows from alternative depots and adjust convoy plans. Apply shortage penalties in accordance with operational priority tiers and push immediate resupply as conditions permit.
